question: Under polarised light microscopy, calcium pyrophosphate dehydrate (CPPD) crystals seen in pseudogout are positively birefringent (appear blue when aligned parallel to the slow axis of the compensator), while monosodium urate crystals in gout are negatively birefringent.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. CPPD crystals are POSITIVELY birefringent (blue parallel to the slow axis); monosodium urate crystals are NEGATIVELY birefringent (yellow parallel to the slow axis). Additionally, gout crystals are needle-shaped while CPPD crystals are rhomboid.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The birefringence mnemonic: gout = Negative birefringence, CPPD (pseudogout) = Positive birefringence. Crystal morphology also differs: urate crystals are needle-shaped; CPPD crystals are rhomboid/rectangular.
